children.text: CHERENKOV LIGHT AND RING IMAGING COUNTER

A charged particle travels at \(v=\beta c>c/n\) in a transparent medium of index n. Its Cherenkov light makes angle \(\theta=\arccos[1/(\beta n)]\) with its trajectory. Keep only the requested small-angle terms in \(\theta\) and mirror-axis tilt \(\alpha\). In a ring-imaging Cherenkov counter, the beam crosses a concave spherical mirror at S. Its centre is C, focal length f, and the beam line IS makes small angle alpha with SC. Numerical momenta are in GeV/c and rest masses in GeV/\(c^2\).

nodes.alt: Original particle path from A to B and rays making Cherenkov angle theta with the trajectory.

children.text: 1.1. Wavefront construction
A particle passes A at time zero and B at time \(t_1\), emitting spherical waves along the path at speed \(c/n\). Draw the envelope at \(t_1\) in a plane containing AB.
1.2. Wavefront cone angle
Find the angle \(\varphi\) between a side of this wavefront cone and the particle trajectory.
2. Ring centre and radius
Use a ray sketch to explain the ring image and find its centre O and radius.
3.1. Threshold radiator pressures

A beam with momentum 10.0 GeV/c contains protons, kaons and pions of masses 0.94, 0.50 and 0.14 GeV/\(c^2\). Air has \(n=1+aP\), \(a=2.7\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{atm^{-1}}\). Find the threshold pressures for each species.
3.2.pressure. Half-radius kaon ring
Find pressure \(P_{1/2}\) such that the kaon ring radius is half the pion ring radius.
3.2.angles. Ring angles and proton visibility
At that pressure find both angles, and determine whether protons make a ring.
4.1. Momentum-to-angle width
At \(P_{1/2}\), the momentum distribution is centred on 10 GeV/c with half width at half height \(\Delta p\). Find \(\Delta\theta_K/\Delta p\) and \(\Delta\theta_\pi/\Delta p\).
4.2. Resolvable momentum width
Require \(\theta_\pi-\theta_K>10(\Delta\theta_K+\Delta\theta_\pi)\). Find the largest permitted momentum half width.
5.1. Water radiation threshold
For water with n = 1.33, find threshold kinetic energy for rest mass M.
5.2. Radioactive particles

Find threshold energies for alpha particles of mass 3.8 GeV/\(c^2\) and electrons of mass 0.51 MeV/\(c^2\). A radioactive source emits particles with at most a few MeV. Which species explains Cherenkov's observed water light?
6.1. Chromatic angular spread

Visible wavelengths span 0.4 to 0.8 micrometres. Across this range n decreases linearly by 2 percent of \(n-1\). For 10 GeV/c pions in air at 6 atm, find the angular difference between the two ends of the visible spectrum.
6.2.1. Two broadening mechanisms
The pion momentum half width is now 0.3 GeV/c at a centre of 10 GeV/c. Estimate ring broadening from dispersion and from momentum spread, using half-width conventions.
6.2.2. Ring colour ordering
Describe colour from the inner edge to the outer edge.

children.text: CHERENKOV LIGHT AND RING IMAGING COUNTER
1.1. Wavefront construction

Every emitted sphere has radius \((c/n)(t_1-t)\), proportional to its centre's distance \(v(t_1-t)\) behind B. The common tangent envelope is a cone with vertex B. In the selected plane its two sides are straight tangent lines extending backwards from B. Draw the endpoint cap if restricting emission to the finite segment AB.
1.2. Wavefront cone angle
The right triangle between B, a wave centre and its tangent point gives \(\sin\varphi=1/(\beta n)\). Thus \(\varphi=\arcsin[1/(\beta n)]=\pi/2-\theta\).
2. Ring centre and radius

Parallel Cherenkov rays at a given azimuth focus to one point of the focal plane. Their fixed angle theta around IS generates a circle. The line through C parallel to IS intersects that plane at O. If F is the axial focus, \(FO=f\alpha\) to first order, and ring radius \(r=f\theta\). The ray diagram must show these constructions.
3.1. Threshold radiator pressures

With \(K=Mc/p\), \(\beta=1/\sqrt{1+K^2}\). The exact threshold is \(P_{min}=(\sqrt{1+K^2}-1)/a\), approximately \(K^2/(2a)\). This gives about 16 atm for protons, 4.6 atm for kaons and 0.36 atm for pions. Radiation requires pressure above the threshold.
3.2.pressure. Half-radius kaon ring
For small theta and small \(n-1\), \(\theta^2\simeq2aP-K^2\). Set \(\theta_\pi=2\theta_K\), giving \[aP_{1/2}=\frac{4K_K^2-K_\pi^2}{6}.\] The pressure is about 6.0 atm.
3.2.angles. Ring angles and proton visibility

The angles are \(\theta_K\simeq0.0277\,\mathrm{rad}=1.6^\circ\), \(\theta_\pi\simeq0.0554\,\mathrm{rad}=3.2^\circ\). Protons do not radiate because this pressure is below their approximately 16 atm threshold.
4.1. Momentum-to-angle width

Differentiate \(\cos\theta=1/(n\beta)\) at fixed n. To leading order, \[\frac{d\theta}{dp}\simeq\frac{K^2}{\theta p}.\] The values are about \(0.51^\circ/(\mathrm{GeV}/c)\) for kaons and \(0.020^\circ/(\mathrm{GeV}/c)\) for pions.
4.2. Resolvable momentum width
The angular separation is about \(1.6^\circ\) and the sum-width coefficient is \(0.53^\circ/(\mathrm{GeV}/c)\). Therefore \(\Delta p<1.6/(10\times0.53)\simeq0.30\,\mathrm{GeV}/c\).
5.1. Water radiation threshold
At threshold \(\beta=1/n\). Relativistic kinetic energy gives \[T_{min}=Mc^2\left[\frac1{\sqrt{1-1/n^2}}-1\right]\simeq0.517Mc^2.\]
5.2. Radioactive particles
Thresholds are \(1.96\,\mathrm{GeV}\) for alpha particles and \(0.264\,\mathrm{MeV}\) for electrons. Only electrons can exceed their threshold at the given radioactive energies.
6.1. Chromatic angular spread

\(\delta n=0.02(n-1)\), and differentiating the Cherenkov relation gives \(\delta\theta=\delta n/(n\tan\theta)\simeq\delta n/\theta\). With \(n=1.00162\), \(\theta\simeq0.055\,\mathrm{rad}\), this is \(0.033^\circ\).
6.2.1. Two broadening mechanisms

The full visible angular spread from 6.1 corresponds to an approximate dispersion half width \(0.017^\circ\). Momentum spread contributes \(0.020\times0.3=0.006^\circ\). Dispersion is about three times larger. The source treats the spectral half-span as a half-width estimate, not a specified exact spectral line shape.
6.2.2. Ring colour ordering
Long-wavelength red light has lower n and smaller theta. Short-wavelength blue/violet light has larger theta. The ordering is red, then a white overlap region, then blue/violet at the outside.
